checks: Every selected group has positive section sum from an interior anchor. With the displayed weights, the rho-weighted threshold changes sum to zero. Thus the original assigned whole-base-plane covers persist. Finite old slack covers also persist under continuous cap masses.

If all group responses were negative the shifted caps would each fall below the new normalized budget. Separation from the open negative orthant produces one probability vector, independent of the tested support paths. Signed directions give equality and one-sided contraction directions give the stated convex-order sign.

Smooth localization gives the mass, base and physical-point moments everywhere on each regular incidence patch. For each fixed convex test a negative value would persist on an open patch, so there is no uncountable intersection of full-measure sets.

The row polytope is compact and contains the diagonal array before column masses are imposed. The separating-cost lower envelope is finite max-affine on the finite hull, so convex order forces the desired column vector. The anchored support gap is globally nonnegative and vanishes at that normal, so its first spherical derivative also vanishes and gives the full physical barycenter.

At a vertex of a nonempty bounded feasible polytope the positive columns are independent. Extending to a full-rank minor and testing the entire system makes the first feasible basic array a Borel choice even as the rank changes. Row and column identities integrate and give the full conditional barycenter.

Subtracting the limiting moment equations gives the signed jump equation. A strict affine separator puts every signed jump term on the same nonnegative side, and all relevant Gauss Jacobians and within-group weights are positive.

Original 833ec49c5d634bf9 §§4–5, 7–10 contains the stress, physical lift and separate measurable-choice argument. The scope remains any selected complete cover at a smooth positively curved local minimum.
